one_line_description.value: DealCloud is a deal-and-pipeline management platform used for relationship and pipeline insights, diligence and meeting preparation.
one_line_description.quote: The DealCloud MCP Server helps teams turn their DealCloud data into faster, higher-quality outcomes. AI assistants can surface sharper relationship and pipeline insights, prepare teams for diligence and meetings, then act on what they find

has_public_api.quote: Welcome to the DealCloud API Docs! This site provides a comprehensive overview of our REST APIs, their capabilities, and available endpoints.

api_type.quote: This site provides a comprehensive overview of our REST APIs, their capabilities, and available endpoints.

api_breadth.value: REST, 7 functional API areas with multiple endpoints each (authentication, user management, schema, data, backups, publications, relationship intelligence)
api_breadth.quote: Our APIs are organized into functional areas. Each area includes multiple endpoints designed to help you perform specific tasks related to that category.

docs_url.quote: Whether you're building custom integrations, automating workflows, or exploring advanced use cases, you'll find detailed guidance, examples, and best practices throughout.

auth_methods.quote: DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token, which is then used in the HTTP Authentication header for API requests.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: When generating a token, use one or more scopes listed below, separated by a space. It is recommended to include only the scopes needed.

access_model.quote: To enable API access, ensure the intended user is assigned to a user group with the appropriate permissions. Navigate to Admin > User Management, select the relevant user group, go to Capabilities > Site Areas, and enable "API".

access_notes.value: Requires an existing DealCloud site (enterprise customer) where a site admin has assigned the user to a group with the "API" capability; credentials are an OAuth2 client_id/client_secret plus the user's API key used to mint bearer tokens (tokens expire after 900 seconds). MCP requires a Celeste license and "Manage MCP Servers"/"MCP Access" capabilities. No free developer edition, trial, or self-serve signup is documented in the supplied evidence.
access_notes.quote: If you do not see the Admin section, contact your organization's admin or DealCloud Customer Success Manager (CSM) for assistance.

official_mcp_server.quote: DealCloud provides a default MCP Server out-of-the-box without any configuration required. It exposes your site's full schema and is the fastest way to get connected. Copy the MCP endpoint URL from Tools > MCP Servers and connect it to your AI client.

rate_limits.value: Endpoint-based quotas: OAuth token 300 per minute; user management, data, schema and RelIntel 5 per second
rate_limits.quote: | Authentication | /api/rest/v1/oauth/token | 300 per minute | | User Management | /api/rest/v1/management | 5 per second | | Data | /api/rest/v4/data | 5 per second | | Schema | /api/rest/v4/schema | 5 per second | | RelIntel | /api/rest/v4/ri/import | 5 per second |

webhooks.quote: Subscribe to change events from DealCloud via the Publications API. The SDK exposes topic discovery, long-poll (`poll_events` / `stream_poll_events`), acknowledgement, bootstrap, and blocking `subscribe` / `subscribe_async` helpers.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Path-versioned REST: /api/rest/v1 for user management (and auth/publications) versus /api/rest/v4 for data and schema; no formal deprecation/sunset policy found in the supplied docs.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: | user_management | Required when accessing the User Management API endpoints (api/rest/v1/management) | | data | Required when accessing the Data or Schema API endpoints (api/rest/v4/data or api/rest/v4/schema). |

verdict_reason: DealCloud publishes thorough REST API docs with OAuth2 client-credentials bearer tokens, a documented scope model, per-endpoint rate limits, and an out-of-the-box MCP server. However, credentials only exist inside an existing DealCloud site: a site admin must enable the "API" capability on the user's group, and the MCP server requires a Celeste license. No self-serve developer signup, trial, or sandbox is documented, so access is gated rather than open.
main_blocker: Requires an existing DealCloud site plus site-admin-enabled API capability; no self-serve developer tier documented
open_questions: Can a free, trial, or sandbox DealCloud site be provisioned self-serve? No pricing/plans page or sandbox page was captured in the evidence.
How are OAuth2 client_id/client_secret provisioned (site admin console vs DealCloud support)? Not documented in the supplied sources.
The SDKs index page implies multiple SDKs, but only the Python dealcloud_sdk is evidenced here; are other official vendor SDKs offered?
Publications API delivers change events via long-poll rather than HTTP webhooks; confirm whether any webhook/callback mechanism exists.
The API reference exists at /releases and SDK changelogs in the search index, but no formal versioning/deprecation/sunset policy text was captured.
No community/third-party MCP servers were found (MCP registry and GitHub checks returned no results); the checks may have been incomplete.
The one_line_description was inferred from the MCP/product-domain page because no general product overview page was fetched.
API behavior is per-site (Swagger at https://{{host}}/swagger); per-tenant differences in schema and available endpoints are unknown.
MCP endpoint is per-tenant (https://[tenant].my.intapp.com/mcp/celeste/DealCloud), so the value points at the documented format rather than a single fixed URL.
